quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which color is best to wear so others can see you?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green while riding. These colors make you easier to see at any time of day.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT help protect you from serious injury?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots that support your ankles, and gloves made of durable material. Ear buds do not protect you.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly
Shift your weight toward the good tire
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep going straight. Gradually brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, what should you do?

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual
Start slowing down later than usual
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly
Brake lighter than usual to protect the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual
questions.explanation: A passenger in a sidecar adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will need more space to stop.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good idea if your friend has been drinking?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them
Keep them busy with other activities
Keep them from leaving until they are sober

questions.explanation: Prevent an impaired friend from riding by arranging another way home, keeping them busy, and stopping them from leaving until they are sober. Never let them ride their motorcycle.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will usually not hear a tire going flat. Instead, notice a sudden change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: Which will NOT reduce your chances of crashing?

options.text: Wear bright clothing and use your headlight
Use turn signals and brake lights to show your intentions
Look for hazards in your path

questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, make sure other drivers can see you, tell them what you plan to do, and keep space around you. Search for and avoid hazards. Be ready to react to anything.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After at least one hour of riding
After more than eight hours of riding

questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after starting to ride.

questions.question: If a dog chases you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for it to lose interest

questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. Downshift and slow down as you approach the dog. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: What can help if your drive chain slips?
questions.explanation: If the chain slips, try tightening it. If this does not fix the problem, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: To work well, a face shield should NOT:

options.text: Allow clear views to both sides.

questions.explanation: A face shield should let air pass through. An airtight shield can cause fogging and make it hard to see. A good face shield should be scratch-free, block impacts, allow side vision, fit securely, and leave room for glasses underneath.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across the surface.
Tighten your hold on the handle grips and increase your speed to get past the hazard.
Ride on the shoulder instead of on the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across the surface.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Simply relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Ride in a position that will allow the other driver to see you in their rearview mirror.
Ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a position that will allow the other driver to see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Riding in the center of the lane usually puts you in the middle of their mirror, where they are most likely to see you.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect your body?

options.text: They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, and allergies make you drowsy and reduce your ability to ride safely. Know how any medication affects you before you ride.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before starting your motorcycle. Adjust them so you can see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of an accident, you should:

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Not look ahead and focus only on your controls.
Communicate your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to others. Signal your turns, use your brake light, and position yourself correctly. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Rely on your mirrors to show you all of your surroundings.
Point in the direction of the lane change.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Mirrors alone are not enough.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should use both brakes:

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Only when riding in the city.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the best stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated by:
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down to approach the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to approach the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and slow down as you approach it. Once you are close, speed up and leave it behind. Do not kick the dog.

questions.question: Which choice best protects your eyes from wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Most windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide good eye protection from wind.
